Lessons.Title: Multiples of 100
ExplanationParagraphs: Multiples of 100: students explore how numbers lie between and near multiples of one hundred and learn to choose the nearest multiple of 100 from a number line. Correct the inherited catalogue suffix 'PLC Activity': the original 2021 student and teacher lesson is titled Multiples of 100.

Warm-up — Estimation Exploration: Marching Band (10 minutes). View the original 2007 marching-band photograph with your teacher, then propose and justify three estimates: too low, about right, too high. There is no single exact count given by the source. People may differ over whether they include only uniformed performers or everyone on the field. Do not auto-grade the crowd size from an invented value.

Activity 1 — About 100? Close to 100? (10 minutes). Original school counts are playground 94, cafeteria 163, art room 36, library 13, classrooms 216, gymnasium 109 and music room 52. First decide which are 'about 100' and explain why. Then sort into 'close to 0', 'close to 100', 'close to 200', or set aside numbers that do not seem close.

The publisher explicitly DOES NOT define a numerical threshold for 'close to' during Activity 1. For instance 52 is mathematically nearer to 100 than 0, but it is near the middle and a pupil may argue it is not close to either endpoint. Do not replace this teacher-led reasoning activity with automatic conventional rounding.

Activity 2 — Close to Multiples of 100 (25 minutes). The source assigns group A: 94,36,109,163,229; group B: 24,52,216,11,481; group C: 187,135,67,83,241; group D: 332,154,408,296,45; or group E: 279,205,377,449,73. Each group locates and labels its five numbers on hundred-to-hundred number lines, then records the nearest hundred for each number.

Use place-value number-line intervals from 0 to 100,100 to 200,200 to 300,300 to 400 and400 to 500. Place 364 between 300 and400. It is64 above300 and36 below400, so 400 is the nearer multiple. Two enclosing multiples can be named even when one is not the nearest.

Group D nearest hundreds:332→300,154→200,408→400,296→300,45→0. Group E:279→300,205→200,377→400,449→400,73→100. These are mathematically nearest-hundred anchors for the source Group A–E task, not a machine-graded substitute for drawing a located point, explaining distance, or the subjective Activity 1 'close to' classification.

For the lesson synthesis, compare numbers that share the nearest hundred although their exact values differ:67 and135 both have nearest hundred100; 449 is only49 away from400 and51 away from500. A number can be closer to an endpoint while still sounding quite far from it in everyday speech.

Edulytics independent practice asks whether 229 is nearer200 than300, and the independent Cool-down rounds481 to500, while teacher separately checks group number lines, class estimation and reasoning. The publisher restricted original Locate, Label, and Name Cool-down and licensed source photographs are not reproduced.

KeyConcepts.Title: Multiples of 100
KeyConcepts.Definition: 0, 100, 200, 300, 400, 500 and so on are multiples of 100.
KeyConcepts.Rule: Find the two enclosing multiples of 100 by reading the hundreds interval.

KeyConcepts.Title: Nearest multiple
KeyConcepts.Definition: The multiple of 100 with the smaller distance from a given number.
KeyConcepts.Rule: Compare the distances to the lower and upper endpoints; for 364,64 vs36 means400.
KeyConcepts.Example: 449 lies49 from400 and51 from500, so400 is nearer.

KeyConcepts.Title: About versus closer to
KeyConcepts.Definition: 'Close to' in the initial informal task has no fixed threshold. 'Closer to' explicitly compares two distances.
KeyConcepts.Rule: Do not use an unannounced machine-graded cutoff for the original subjective sorting discussion.
KeyConcepts.Example: 52 is mathematically closer to100 than0 but may not feel close to either.

KeyConcepts.Title: Visual number-line reasoning
KeyConcepts.Definition: A number's relative position on an interval explains why a specific hundred is nearest.
KeyConcepts.Rule: Draw a point, label its hundred interval and explain how far it is from endpoints.

WorkedExamples.Title: Estimate without pretending to count exactly
WorkedExamples.Question: How many people could be in the marching-band photograph?
WorkedExamples.Method: Make and justify a low, reasonable and high estimate.
Steps: Decide whether you are counting only band performers or everyone on the field.
Group visually into tens or hundreds to form a reasonable estimate.
Propose one clearly too low and one clearly too high estimate around the about-right value.
Discuss evidence with your teacher; the source has no official exact numeric answer.
WorkedExamples.Answer: Teacher review; no single scalar answer.
WorkedExamples.Check: Compare who was counted and the magnitude.

WorkedExamples.Title: Use the nearest hundred for an assigned source number
WorkedExamples.Question: For source group B, which hundred is nearest to481?
WorkedExamples.Check: 481 rounds to500 to the nearest hundred.

CommonMistakes.Mistake: Treating 'about100' and 'mathematically nearer to100' as synonyms.
CommonMistakes.WhyWrong: Original Activity1 permits flexible, explained judgments without a threshold.
CommonMistakes.Correction: Discuss 52 in both contexts and do not auto-score the original subjective table.

CommonMistakes.Mistake: Claiming the band photograph contains exactly a fixed number of people.
CommonMistakes.WhyWrong: The source deliberately asks for estimates and whether to include people on or off the band group.
CommonMistakes.Correction: Require too low, about right and too high estimates with supporting reasons.

CommonMistakes.Mistake: Rounding 449 to500 because it is close to450.
CommonMistakes.Correction: Use the actual distances and round to400.

CommonMistakes.Mistake: Naming only the nearest hundred for364 and omitting its containing interval.
CommonMistakes.WhyWrong: The original asks for two multiples enclosing the number and which is nearer.
CommonMistakes.Correction: Give300 and400, then explain why400 is nearer.

CommonMistakes.Mistake: Using a true nearest-hundred answer as proof of having placed a source number line point.
CommonMistakes.WhyWrong: The original activity also assesses visual representation, estimation and collaboration.
CommonMistakes.Correction: Teacher independently checks diagrams, group work and reasoning.

SummaryPoints: 2021 original title Multiples of 100, not Multiples of 100 PLC Activity.
Source grouping A–E includes25 separate numerical entries, each mapped to nearest hundred.
364 has enclosing hundreds300 and400 and nearest400.
The original 'close to' discussion has no official numeric threshold; it remains teacher-scored.
Independent Edulytics source-goal equivalent Cool-down rounds481 to500; source publisher images and gated assessment not copied.
